column1: # Curated help for the keys worth explaining. Hand-written, and deliberately NOT
# produced by gen-schema.py: that file is regenerated from a device and would
# overwrite anything written here. Merged with it by name, in the browser.
# Everything below is sourced from the device itself — /etc/runomci.sh for how a
# key reaches omci_app, and measurement for the rest. Where a claim is not
# grounded it says so rather than guessing.
# depends  KEY=VALUE, joined by &. When unmet the UI says the key is ignored,
#          because that is what the firmware does with it.

column3: help

Becomes `omci_app -t`. Anything outside the listed values falls back to bridge. Switching between HGU and SFU also needs a CS factory reset — this key alone leaves a stale WAN entry behind and the ONU keeps running as a router.
Selects which VLAN path omci_app takes. 1 gives `-iot_vt 1`; every other value gives `-iot_vt 0`, and the manual VLAN fields below are ignored entirely.
Only read when VLAN config mode is 1. Mode 1 passes the VLAN ID and priority below to omci_app; any other value sends the 65535/255 sentinels instead, which means the VLAN ID is ignored.
column4: 0=0 — off|1=1 — tag using the VLAN ID below

column3: The C-VLAN the ONU tags upstream traffic with — your ISP's service VLAN. Used only when VLAN config mode is 1 AND manual VLAN mode is 1. If this or the priority is left empty, runomci.sh drops the whole -iot_ block and no VLAN configuration reaches omci_app at all.
802.1p priority bits carried in the tag. Same gating as the VLAN ID, and equally must not be empty.

Hex bitmask, passed as `omci_app -cr`. Bit 0x4 suppresses the ME 171 uniNode association check; both of our sticks run 4. On the 2024 firmware that same bit also skips populating the resolved association, which stops the ONU forwarding at all.
Hex bitmask, passed as `omci_app -cb`.
Hex bitmask, passed as `omci_app -cme`.
Hex bitmask, passed as `omci_app -cmc`.
1 starts omci_app with `-m enable_wq`.
Answers OK to OMCI operations the stack cannot actually satisfy. Some OLTs refuse to finish provisioning without it.
Read by boa, configd, led, mib and xmlconfig — and NOT by omci_app or checkomci. It does not affect provisioning, which was confirmed from the binaries rather than assumed.
Passed to omci_app. 255 is the default here; the OLT bridges to the VEIP rather than the physical UNI on both of our lines.
The address this UI, SSH and telnet answer on. Changing it drops your session.
Handed to the europa driver at boot by insert_europa.sh.
What the OLT authenticates. Four-character vendor prefix followed by eight hex digits. Lose it and the ONU will not come up on the line.
The first four characters of the serial number, and must match it.
32 hex characters.
eth0 comes up with this address.
Reported to the OLT in the ONU-G managed entity.
Stored as the hex of an ASCII string, shown decoded above. Many OLTs authenticate on the serial number alone and leave this empty — one of ours does, the other uses it.
1 on both of our lines.
The device login for SSH and telnet. Not this UI's password, which lives in /etc/config/confd.auth.
The device login for SSH and telnet.
